policy.rule: A candidate disposition controls verification workflow only; it never creates linguistic authority.
policy.closedMeaning: Reviewed and intentionally not published as an independent learner morpheme.
policy.deferredMeaning: Potentially meaningful, but insufficient evidence or product value to publish now.

decisions.reason: Latin pono directly supports PON/PONE/POSIT. POS alone is an arbitrary pedagogical truncation of posui/positum rather than a separately attested source-language morpheme; LexiFlow will teach the evidenced forms instead.
Allen & Greenough explicitly analyzes mitt-i-tis with root MIT and consonant doubling in the present stem. MITT is therefore a stem spelling effect, not a separate root.

Latin misi is part of the mittere paradigm, but publishing learner-facing MIS would collide with the unrelated English/Germanic mis- prefix. MIT/MISS plus the verified MISE transmission provide a safer teaching model.

TIN appears in traditional pedagogical groupings around teneo compounds, but LexiFlow requires a separately documented compound-stem/vowel-change rule before publishing it as an independent teaching form. TEN/TENT authority and TAIN transmission are already available.

Latin authority already has VIV from vivo/vivus. The sequence vivi- is not required as a separate learner morpheme; publishing it would duplicate an inflected/derived surface sequence rather than add a distinct source-language fact.
Lewis & Short explicitly derives vitalis from vita. LexiFlow therefore keeps VITA as the source-language authority form instead of publishing the pedagogical truncation VIT.
Latin pes, pedis directly supports PED as the source-language stem. PEDI is not needed as an independent morpheme record; word-level analysis can link relevant forms back to PED.

Latin pes, pedis directly supports PED. The learner form PEDE is a downstream word-shape/pedagogical variant rather than a separately attested source-language morpheme, so it is intentionally not published.
Latin facio and compounds directly support FAC/FACT/FIC/FECT-related branches, while FEC is only a truncation of forms such as feci and does not add a distinct learner morpheme.
Latin cedo directly gives cessi/cessum, so CESS is the evidenced source-language branch. CES is an unnecessary truncation and is not published separately.
Greek βίος supports BIO through βιο-. BI is not needed as an independent life-morpheme and would create ambiguity with unrelated bi- formations.
Greek βίος supports BIO through the attested/grammatical βιο- stem. BE is not a separately justified Greek morpheme in this family and is intentionally not published.

EPI- is source-language verified from Ancient Greek ἐπί. EPH- reflects phonological/elision behavior around ἐφ᾽, but LexiFlow will not publish it until an approved Greek grammar source is attached to the exact variant rule.

EPI- is source-language verified from Ancient Greek ἐπί. EP- is a reduced/elided surface form; it remains deferred until the approved grammar layer explicitly documents the contraction/elision environment.

The indexed candidate cap2 denotes the CAPUT 'head' family, not CAP < capio 'take'. LexiFlow publishes the evidenced source forms CAPIT/CIPIT and intentionally does not publish ambiguous CAP for the head family.

decisions.candidateId: ecdict:cur1, curr, cor1, corr, curs, cour1, cours
decisions.reason: COUR is an arbitrary truncation of later French/English forms such as courier/course. COURS has a specific historical transmission mapping; COUR is intentionally not published.

Latin moveo directly supports MOV/MOT through moveo/movi/motum. MOB is a pedagogical truncation associated with later mobilis/mobile forms, not a separately attested source-language root in this family; LexiFlow therefore keeps MOV/MOT and does not publish MOB as an independent morpheme.

The ECDICT discovery row labels MIS- as Latin, but authoritative Old English evidence shows mis- is a Germanic/Old English prefix denoting defect or imperfection. LexiFlow publishes MIS- from Old English authority and closes this specific Latin-classified discovery candidate so a wrong origin hint cannot be counted as verified coverage.
